# `sesam add --nested` gives a subdirectory its own sesam.yml and includes it
# from the main file. git never descends into an ignored directory, so the
# generated .gitignore has to unignore directories (`!*/`) for its `!sesam.yml`
# to reach one: without that, `git add -A` skipped every sub-config in silence
# and the file - comments, anchors and all - lived in the worktree only.

sesam-repo

mkdir svc
cp token svc/token.txt
exec sesam add --nested svc/token.txt
exists svc/sesam.yml

# Depth is not the point: the negation is not anchored, so it matches anywhere.
mkdir deep/nested
cp token deep/nested/key.txt
exec sesam add --nested deep/nested/key.txt
exists deep/nested/sesam.yml

# The sub-configs are committable...
! exec git check-ignore svc/sesam.yml
! exec git check-ignore deep/nested/sesam.yml

# ...while the revealed plaintext next to them, and sesam's own scratch dir,
# stay ignored - that part is what the blanket `*` is there for.
exec git check-ignore svc/token.txt
exec git check-ignore deep/nested/key.txt
exec git check-ignore .sesam/tmp/svc/token.txt.ours

exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add nested secrets'

exec git ls-files
stdout '^svc/sesam\.yml$'
stdout '^deep/nested/sesam\.yml$'
! stdout '^svc/token\.txt$'
! stdout '^deep/nested/key\.txt$'

# The declaration matches the audit log, so a reset has nothing to discard and
# leaves both sub-configs where they are.
exec sesam config reset
stdout 'nothing to reset'
exists svc/sesam.yml
exists deep/nested/sesam.yml

-- token --
s3cr3t
